doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Struggling without goals or deadlines; recording projects and arrangements
summary: She says she does not work well without deadlines; Arbors and Venus Records asked for projects, and Monk mentions writing for his sax ensemble.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Some people do very well when they have time to do other things.
Not me either. It’s amazing how little you can do with so much time.

It’s crazy, isn’t it? I mean I’m mad at myself that I don’t have a great music library all set up. I don’t. It was one of the goals, and I have to get to it. You know what I mean? There’s certain things you have to do. You kind of have piles of music around forever and think that you can be organized that way. It doesn’t work. And I don’t know when — earlier in the year Arbors Records and Venus Records both asked me to do a project, a recording project. That means writing arrangements. I’ve realized that I really don’t work well without a goal, without a deadline. It’s hard for me to work — I don’t know what the first gig is going to be and who with, or the first series of gigs. So I almost sometimes don’t know what to practice. It’s crazy.
You know I’ve been writing music for my college saxophone ensemble. I don’t know if they’re coming back yet.
My sister sent that chart, I’ll remind her if she didn’t send the “Waltzing Matilda” chart.
